label: mid original-phase steps after several s/z/w/l/n/k/b/2 inputs
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase (95% of mass), at positions t=2..6 and peaking at t=3-4. It never fires at t=0, almost never on the delimiter, and only weakly in the copy phase. Within that window, how often and how strongly it fires depends on which tokens came before: the rate is about 3x when s, z, w, l or n (and to a lesser degree k, b, 2) were among the previous one or two inputs or were the first token. Requiring at least two such earlier tokens gives dev F1 0.47 (precision 0.39, recall 0.60, mass recall 0.74). The input token itself also raises the activation: x has 5x lift and gives the strongest activations (near max right after s/z/w/n prefixes, e.g. s z w [x]), and l and f also raise it. The feature fires more on the first occurrence of a token than on a repeat. The structure looks like a graded, additive weighting of tokens over a short window rather than a crisp rule, so precision stays low.
